rename.resolution: Re-verdicted rename -> declined; there is no ours-half, so the suffix question it was blocked on does not arise. Consistent with cpp:Subscription::take_type_erased. No code change; no target name invented.

why:
RE-VERDICTED 2026-08-26 (phase-379 W5), rename -> declined. The blocker asked which suffix ours should carry (`_raw` vs `_serialized` vs `type_erased`); the question was moot, because there is no ours-side method here to suffix.
`ClientBase::take_type_erased_response(void * response_out, rmw_request_id_t & request_header_out)` erases over a DESERIALIZED response STRUCT -- it is the function the typed `Client::take_response` forwards to (`client.hpp:515`). Our C++ client has no such entry point: the reply comes back concretely typed through `Future<ResponseType>` from `Client::async_send_request`. Our only erasure is BYTES (`nros_cpp_service_client_take_response` at `nros_cpp_ffi.h:1651`, `rclc_polling_client_take_response_raw`; both were named here by their pre-W6 spellings until 2026-09-04, phase-417), and those correlate with the SERIALIZED/RAW rows, not with this one -- so pointing this row at a `_raw` form was the same mis-pairing that `cpp:Subscription::take_type_erased` had.
Not a gap: a runtime type-erased take needs rosidl typesupport resolved at runtime and a heap-allocated message struct to take into -- exactly what `cpp:Subscription::create_message` declines for the no-allocator reason. Kept consistent with `cpp:Subscription::take_type_erased` (pubsub), decided the same day on the same evidence.
